statement: A 5 by 5 by 5 cube is made of 125 unit cubes. Three straight tunnels are drilled right through it, each removing one full line of unit cubes and joining the centres of two opposite faces: front to back, top to bottom and left to right. How many unit cubes are removed?

choices.misconception: I added the three tunnels of 5 cubes each without noticing that they cross.
I subtracted one cube for each pair of tunnels, but all three pairs share the same single centre cube.
I saw that the centre cube was counted more than once but subtracted it only once, though it was counted three times.
I worked out how many cubes are left in the big cube instead of how many are removed.

hints: Where do the three tunnels meet?
Each tunnel is a line of 5 cubes, but the lines may share cubes. Add the three lines, then correct for any cube you counted more than once.
All three tunnels pass through the very centre cube, and they share no other cube. That cube was counted three times in 5 + 5 + 5.

solutions.reliable: Each tunnel removes a line of 5 unit cubes, and 3 x 5 = 15 counts every removed cube at least once. The three lines all pass through the centre cube of the big cube and share no other cube. The centre cube was counted three times instead of once, so subtract 2: 15 - 2 = 13. The transferable idea: when shapes overlap, count each piece and then fix every cube that was counted more than once.
solutions.elegant: Count the centre cube once, then each tunnel adds the 4 cubes it has besides the centre: 1 + 3 x 4 = 13.

whyOnTest: Counting cubes in a solid tests careful handling of overlaps, and every wrong choice is a different mistake about the shared centre cube.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
